6.2 LONG-TERM PRODUCTIVITY
The 505 acres of terrestrial habitat eliminated by the upper reservoir and appurtenant structures would alter the ecosystem of the area, eliminate the use of the area for future timber or land-oriented wildlife uses, and preclude recreational use. This would continue until such time as conditions similar to those existing now could be reestablished.
Without the proposed action, this environment would continue to provide a habitat capable of supporting a spectrum of deciduous forest biota. Components of this biota include species at the northern or southern limits of their distribution range.
The loss of timber-producing lands on 505 acres could be a long-term adverse effect. Approximately 20 to 30 years would be required before the majority of timber-producing species would be of harvestable size.
Should the proposed project be abandoned, reestablishment of the vegetation types presently in existence on 505 acres (cleared or inundated for the duration of the proposed project) would take many years. Several successional stages would be required. Also, the rare plant species that were eliminated in the reservoir area might never become reestablished within the proposed project area.
